analysis.title: Eq Positioning and Key Levels
key_insights: GS simulates CTAs as sellers of $23bn of SPX over the past week and $46.5bn over the past month. As of Friday's close CTAs are estimated mildly short $3bn of SPX.

SPX price action late last week flipped medium-term momentum positive again, producing modest buying expectations for this week. Spot sits near the threshold level, so the desk expects variable flow forecasts until a clearer trend forms.

GS PB: global equities were net sold (-0.7 SDs, 1-year) as de-grossing increased, with long sales outpacing short covers 2.8 to 1. Single stocks were net sold for a 9th straight week while macro products were net bought for a 4th straight week.
Info Tech was by far the most dollar net sold global and US sector again. The US Info Tech long/short ratio is 1.5 against a YTD peak of 2.14 in early June, the lowest on record (since 2016).

Financials was the most net sold US sector in SD terms (-2.2 SDs, 1-year), with long and short sales at about 4 to 1. The percentage net selling was the largest in 8 months and in the 99th percentile on a 5-year lookback.
Energy was the most dollar net bought and most risk-on global sector, bought at the fastest pace in 3 months with long buys outpacing short sales 7 to 1. Oil, Gas & Consumable Fuels drove the buying.
Consumer Discretionary was the most dollar net bought US sector (+1.0 SDs, 1-year), the largest percentage net buying in more than 3 months, driven by long buys and short covers.
US-listed ETF shorts fell 8.6%, the largest percentage covering in 7 months, led by Large Cap Equity, Credit and Tech ETFs.

Buybacks: about 94% of the S&P 500 is in an open window, rising to about 95% by the end of the week, and the open period is expected to run to early/mid-December. 2026 YTD repurchase authorizations are $1.52T.

Desk buyback execution mix was 45% open market and 55% 10b5-1, versus 33%/67% the prior week. Desk volumes were 1.3x 2025 YTD ADTV and 1.3x 2024 YTD ADTV, skewed to Industrials, Energy and Financials. GS expects the usual December taper.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds were the most net sellers of Info Tech again, and the US long/short ratio fell to 1.5, the lowest since 2016. This describes positioning flows, not a GS rating.
Financials had the largest percentage net selling in 8 months, at -2.2 SDs and the 99th percentile on a 5-year lookback. This describes positioning flows, not a GS rating.
Energy was the most net bought global sector at the fastest pace in 3 months, with long buys outpacing short sales 7 to 1. This describes positioning flows, not a GS rating.
Consumer Discretionary was the most dollar net bought US sector at +1.0 SDs, the largest percentage buying in more than 3 months. This describes positioning flows, not a GS rating.

risk_factors: CTA flow forecasts may vary until a definitive trend is established, because SPX spot sits near the medium-term momentum threshold.
The desk expects a December taper in buyback activity as blackout periods and holiday liquidity constraints set in.
vol_and_positioning: CTA simulation: the cohort sold $23bn of SPX over the past week and $46.5bn over the past month, and is estimated mildly short $3bn of SPX at Friday's close.
CTA flow forecast over the next 1 week: flat tape buyers $22.97B ($9.86B into the US), up tape buyers $30.78B ($16.1B into the US), down tape sellers $6.07B ($5.23B out of the US).
CTA flow forecast over the next 1 month: flat tape buyers $13.87B ($8.01B into the US), up tape buyers $89.1B ($54.04B into the US), down tape sellers $122.97B ($20.31B out of the US).
Key SPX pivot levels: short term 7,657, medium term 7,555, long term 7,133. Data as of 9 Nov 2026. A 1x standard deviation market move is 1.62% in 1 week and 3.78% in 1 month.
GS Equity Fundamental L/S Performance Estimate rose +1.16% between 11/6 and 11/12 against MSCI World TR +2.34%, driven by beta of +1.45% and partly offset by alpha of -0.29% on long side losses.
GS Equity Systematic L/S Performance Estimate rose +1.42% over the same period, driven by alpha of +1.56% from short side gains and partly offset by beta of -0.15%.
Overall book gross leverage fell 2.1 pts to 312.1% (74th percentile, 1-year). Net leverage fell 0.4 pts to 71.4% (3rd percentile, 1-year). The L/S ratio rose 0.1% to 1.593 (4th percentile, 1-year).

Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 2.6 pts to 208.4% (34th percentile) and net leverage rose 0.1 pts to 45.4% (1-year low). Beta-adjusted gross rose 6.0 pts to 222.6% (11th percentile) and beta-adjusted net fell 0.2 pts to 57.0% (1-year low).
US Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 1.6 pts to 209.1% (34th percentile) and net leverage rose 2.1 pts to 45.4% (4th percentile).

Hedge funds net sold US equities for a second straight week (5 of the last 6, -0.4 SDs, 1-year), through short sales in single stocks partly offset by short covers and long buys in macro products. Single stocks were net sold at -1.7 SDs, mainly through short sales.
